title: ר' שמעון בן רבינו הקדוש

paragraphs:
R' Shimon son of our holy Rabbi: Mishnah Makkot, chapter 3, mishnah 15. He was younger than his brother Rabban Gamliel and greater than he in wisdom. Why was Rabban Gamliel nasi? See his entry. His father entrusted him with the orders of wisdom: Ha-Nose, 103. At the end of Gittin, first chapter, 15a: “R' Shimon the nasi said.” They asked whether he was nasi or spoke in the nasi's name; unresolved. Tosafot write that it is as though it said, “R' Shimon said: the nasi said,” for such is a tanna's manner: “R' Yaakov pays,” as though it said, “R' Yaakov says: he pays.” Sefer Be'er Sheva, Horayot chapter 3, writes that the difference concerns setting his own statements against one another, as at the beginning of Ha-Ish Mekaddesh; see above, R' Avin and Giddel. Rabbi called him “the lamp of Israel,” because he answered his father's objection well: Menahot 88b; Arakhin, chapter 2, 10 beginning of side a. He asked his father: Beitzah, end of Mashillin. Rabbi taught his son R' Shimon: Bava Kamma 111b; Bava Metzia 44a; Avodah Zarah 52b; Horayot 13, end of side b; Bekhorot 5.

He was wiser and greater than R' Hiyya: Tosafot, end of Gittin, 84b. This requires examination; see R' Hiyya. R' Hiyya sat in the bathhouse and did not rise before him. He took offense, saying, “I taught him two fifths of Tehillim, and he did not rise before me.” He likewise took offense at Bar Kappara; some say R' Shmuel—it should read Yishmael—son of R' Yose, who studied two thirds of a third of Torat Kohanim with him and did not rise before him: Kiddushin 33a. He disputes R' Hiyya: Ha-Dar, 72a. His voice was thick, as R' Hiyya told him: Megillah 24b. He was wealthy and miserly; they gave a mnemonic concerning him, “The wealthy are miserly”: Hullin 46a; Menahot 86a. R' Meir was present at the time of his wedding [the Yerushalmi says Meir passed by and heard the clapping], and R' Meir saw him eating in the marketplace; see Rabbi. Bar Kappara wrote on his wedding house, “Twenty-four thousand myriads of dinars were spent, but he did not invite Bar Kappara”: Ha-Noder, 50b; Vayikra Rabbah, chapter 25 [the checked parallel is at 28:2]. He studied with him; see his entry. A daughter was born to him, and he was distressed; his father consoled him: Bava Batra 16b. Batnit said to him. R' Zakkai was his pupil: Yuhasin writes thus, but erred; see his entry. And R' Yannai. Yannai son of R' Yishmael lived in his time. R' Yannai was his son; ל״מ [provisionally: I did not find it]. In R' Yishmael son of R' Yose's name. When Rav Kahana went up, he found R' Shimon son of Rabbi.
